passages.text: Then the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, opposite Jeshimon?”
passages.sermon:
The Ziphites went to Saul.
Saul was at Gibeah.
The Ziphites spoke to Saul.
They said, “David is hiding.”
David is hiding on the hill of Hachilah.
The hill of Hachilah is opposite Jeshimon.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ הַזִּפִים֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל הַגִּבְעָ֖תָה לֵאמֹ֑ר הֲל֨וֹא דָוִ֤ד מִסְתַּתֵּר֙ בְּגִבְעַ֣ת הַחֲכִילָ֔ה עַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הַיְשִׁימֹֽן׃

passages.text: So Saul, accompanied by three thousand chosen men of Israel, went down to the Wilderness of Ziph to search for David there.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul chose three thousand men from Israel.
These men were the best young men of Israel.
Saul took these men with him.
Saul went down to the Wilderness of Ziph.
Saul went there to search for David.
Saul and his men looked for David in the Wilderness of Ziph.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם שָׁא֗וּל וַיֵּ֙רֶד֙ אֶל־ מִדְבַּר־ זִ֔יף וְאִתּ֛וֹ שְׁלֹֽשֶׁת־ אֲלָפִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ בְּחוּרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־ דָּוִ֖ד בְּמִדְבַּר־ זִֽיף׃

passages.text: Saul camped beside the road at the hill of Hachilah opposite Jeshimon, but David was living in the wilderness. When he realized that Saul had followed him there, David sent out spies to verify that Saul had arrived.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul camped beside the road.
He camped at the hill of Hachilah.
This hill was opposite Jeshimon.
David was not with Saul.
David was living in the wilderness.
David saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.
David sent out spies.
The spies checked if Saul had really arrived.
David learned that Saul had come to that place.
passages.original: וַיִּ֨חַן שָׁא֜וּל בְּגִבְעַ֣ת הַחֲכִילָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֛ר עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הַיְשִׁימֹ֖ן עַל־ הַדָּ֑רֶךְ וְדָוִד֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיַּ֕רְא כִּ֣י בָ֥א שָׁא֛וּל אַחֲרָ֖יו הַמִּדְבָּֽרָה׃ וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֖ד מְרַגְּלִ֑ים וַיֵּ֕דַע כִּֽי־ בָ֥א שָׁא֖וּל אֶל־ נָכֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Then David set out and went to the place where Saul had camped. He saw the place where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the general of his army, had lain down. Saul was lying inside the inner circle of the camp, with the troops camped around him.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader and a servant of God.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Abner was the son of Ner and the commander of Saul’s army.
David got up.
David went to the place where Saul had camped.
David saw where Saul was lying down.
David saw Abner, the general, lying there too.
Saul was lying inside the inner circle of the camp.
The troops were camped all around Saul.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וַיָּבֹא֮ אֶֽל־ הַמָּקוֹם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָנָה־ שָׁ֣ם שָׁאוּל֒ וַיַּ֣רְא דָּוִ֗ד אֶת־ הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָֽׁכַב־ שָׁ֣ם שָׁא֔וּל וְאַבְנֵ֥ר בֶּן־ נֵ֖ר שַׂר־ צְבָא֑וֹ וְשָׁאוּל֙ שֹׁכֵ֣ב בַּמַּעְגָּ֔ל וְהָעָ֖ם חֹנִ֥ים סְבִיבֹתוֹ׃

passages.text: And David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, “Who will go down with me to Saul in the camp?” “I will go with you,” answered Abishai.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader and a servant of God.
Ahimelech was a Hittite.
Abishai was the son of Zeruiah.
Joab was Abishai’s brother.
David spoke to Ahimelech and Abishai.
David said, “Who will go down with me to Saul in the camp?”
Abishai answered David.
Abishai said, “I will go with you.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן דָּוִ֜ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ אֶל־ אֲחִימֶ֣לֶךְ הַחִתִּ֗י וְאֶל־ אֲבִישַׁ֨י בֶּן־ צְרוּיָ֜ה אֲחִ֤י יוֹאָב֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מִֽי־ יֵרֵ֥ד אִתִּ֛י אֶל־ שָׁא֖וּל אֶל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִישַׁ֔י אֲנִ֖י אֵרֵ֥ד עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: That night David and Abishai came to the troops, and Saul was lying there asleep in the inner circle of the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head. And Abner and the troops were lying around him.
passages.sermon:
David was a servant of God.
Abishai was the son of Zeruiah.
That night, David and Abishai went to the camp.
They came to the place where Saul and his men were.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul was lying asleep inside the circle of the camp.
Saul’s spear was stuck in the ground by his head.
Abner was the commander of Saul’s army.
Abner and the soldiers were lying around Saul.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא֩ דָוִ֨ד וַאֲבִישַׁ֥י׀ אֶל־ הָעָם֮ לַיְלָה֒ וְהִנֵּ֣ה שָׁא֗וּל שֹׁכֵ֤ב יָשֵׁן֙ בַּמַּעְגָּ֔ל וַחֲנִית֥וֹ מְעוּכָֽה־ בָאָ֖רֶץ מְרַאֲשֹׁתוֹ וְאַבְנֵ֣ר וְהָעָ֔ם שֹׁכְבִ֖ים סְבִיבֹתוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Abishai said to David, “Today God has delivered your enemy into your hand. Now, therefore, please let me thrust the spear through him into the ground with one stroke. I will not need to strike him twice!”
passages.sermon:
Abishai spoke to David.
Abishai said, “God has given your enemy into your hand today.
Let me strike him with the spear.
I will drive the spear into the ground with one blow.
I will not need to strike him again.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲבִישַׁי֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד סִגַּ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים הַיּ֛וֹם אֶת־ אוֹיִבְךָ֖ בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְעַתָּה֩ אַכֶּ֨נּוּ נָ֜א בַּחֲנִ֤ית וּבָאָ֙רֶץ֙ פַּ֣עַם אַחַ֔ת וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁנֶ֖ה לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But David said to Abishai, “Do not destroy him, for who can lift a hand against the LORD’s anointed and be guiltless?”
passages.sermon:
David was a servant of God.
\r\nAbishai was with David.
\r\nSaul was the LORD’s anointed king.
\r\nDavid spoke to Abishai.
\r\nDavid said, “Do not destroy Saul.”
\r\nDavid said, “No one can harm the LORD’s anointed and be innocent.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל־ אֲבִישַׁ֖י אַל־ תַּשְׁחִיתֵ֑הוּ כִּ֠י מִ֣י שָׁלַ֥ח יָד֛וֹ בִּמְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה וְנִקָּֽה׃פ

passages.text: David added, “As surely as the LORD lives, the LORD Himself will strike him down; either his day will come and he will die, or he will go into battle and perish.
passages.sermon:
David spoke.
David was a servant of God.
David said, "The LORD lives."
The LORD is alive and active.
The LORD has power over life and death.
The LORD Himself will strike Saul down.
Saul is the LORD’s anointed king.
Saul will die when the LORD decides.
Saul may die when his day comes.
Saul may die a natural death.
Saul may die in battle.
Saul may perish in war.
The LORD will decide how and when Saul dies.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ חַי־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אִם־ יְהוָ֖ה יִגָּפֶ֑נּוּ אֽוֹ־ יוֹמ֤וֹ יָבוֹא֙ וָמֵ֔ת א֧וֹ בַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה יֵרֵ֖ד וְנִסְפָּֽה׃

passages.text: But the LORD forbid that I should stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed. Instead, take the spear and water jug by his head, and let us go.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Abishai.
David was a servant of God.
David said, “The LORD forbids me to harm the LORD’s anointed one.
I will not raise my hand against him.
Now, take the spear by his head.
Also, take the water jug by his head.
Let us go.”
passages.original: חָלִ֤ילָה לִּי֙ מֵֽיהוָ֔ה מִשְּׁלֹ֥חַ יָדִ֖י בִּמְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֑ה וְ֠עַתָּה קַח־ נָ֨א אֶֽת־ הַחֲנִ֜ית אֲשֶׁ֧ר מְרַאֲשֹׁתוֹ וְאֶת־ צַפַּ֥חַת הַמַּ֖יִם וְנֵ֥לֲכָה לָּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: So David took the spear and water jug by Saul’s head, and they departed. No one saw them or knew about it, nor did anyone wake up; they all remained asleep, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.
passages.sermon:
David was a servant of God.
Saul was the king of Israel.
David took the spear from beside Saul’s head.
David also took the water jug from beside Saul’s head.
David and his companion left the camp.
No one saw David and his companion.
No one knew what happened.
No one woke up while David was there.
Everyone in the camp was asleep.
The LORD had caused a deep sleep to fall on them.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּח֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶֽת־ הַחֲנִ֜ית וְאֶת־ צַפַּ֤חַת הַמַּ֙יִם֙ מֵרַאֲשֹׁתֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם וְאֵ֣ין רֹאֶה֩ וְאֵ֨ין יוֹדֵ֜עַ וְאֵ֣ין מֵקִ֗יץ כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ יְשֵׁנִ֔ים כִּ֚י תַּרְדֵּמַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה נָפְלָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then David crossed to the other side and stood atop the mountain at a distance; there was a wide gulf between them.
passages.sermon:
David was a servant of God.
David crossed over to the other side.
David stood on top of the mountain.
David stood far away from Saul and his men.
There was a large space between David and them.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר דָּוִד֙ הָעֵ֔בֶר וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד עַל־ רֹאשׁ־ הָהָ֖ר מֵֽרָחֹ֑ק רַ֥ב הַמָּק֖וֹם בֵּינֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And David shouted to the troops and to Abner son of Ner, “Will you not answer me, Abner?” “Who calls to the king?” Abner replied.
passages.sermon:
David was a man chosen by God.
David called out loudly to the people.
David called out to Abner.
Abner was the son of Ner.
David said, “Abner, will you not answer me?”
Abner replied to David.
Abner said, “Who are you who calls to the king?”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א דָוִ֜ד אֶל־ הָעָ֗ם וְאֶל־ אַבְנֵ֤ר בֶּן־ נֵר֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא תַעֲנֶ֖ה אַבְנֵ֑ר וַיַּ֤עַן אַבְנֵר֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר מִ֥י אַתָּ֖ה קָרָ֥אתָ אֶל־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ

passages.text: So David said to Abner, “You are a man, aren’t you? And who in Israel is your equal? Why then did you not protect your lord the king when one of the people came to destroy him?
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Abner.
Abner was the commander of Saul’s army.
David said, “You are a man.
No one in Israel is like you.
Why did you not guard your master, the king?
One of the people came to harm your master, the king.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶל־ אַבְנֵ֜ר הֲלוֹא־ אִ֣ישׁ אַתָּ֗ה וּמִ֤י כָמ֙וֹךָ֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלָ֙מָּה֙ לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔רְתָּ אֶל־ אֲדֹנֶ֖יךָ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּי־ בָא֙ אַחַ֣ד הָעָ֔ם לְהַשְׁחִ֖ית אֶת־ הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אֲדֹנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: This thing you have done is not good. As surely as the LORD lives, all of you deserve to die, since you did not protect your lord, the LORD’s anointed. Now look around. Where are the king’s spear and water jug that were by his head?”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Abner and the people.
David said, “This thing you have done is not good.
The LORD lives.
You did not protect your master.
Your master is the LORD’s anointed king.
Because of this, you all deserve to die.
Now look around.
Where is the king’s spear?
Where is the water jug that was by his head?”
passages.original: לֹא־ ט֞וֹב הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּה֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂיתָ֒ חַי־ יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֤י בְנֵי־ מָ֙וֶת֙ אַתֶּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־ שְׁמַרְתֶּ֛ם עַל־ אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֖ם עַל־ מְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֑ה וְעַתָּ֣ה׀ רְאֵ֗ה אֵֽי־ חֲנִ֥ית הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְאֶת־ צַפַּ֥חַת הַמַּ֖יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר מְרַאֲשֹׁתוֹ׃

passages.text: Then Saul recognized David’s voice and asked, “Is that your voice, David my son?” “It is my voice, my lord and king,” David said.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was the son-in-law of Saul.
Saul heard David’s voice.
Saul recognized David’s voice.
Saul asked, “Is that your voice, David my son?”
David answered Saul.
David said, “It is my voice, my lord and king.”
passages.original: וַיַּכֵּ֤ר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־ ק֣וֹל דָּוִ֔ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הֲקוֹלְךָ֥ זֶ֖ה בְּנִ֣י דָוִ֑ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד קוֹלִ֖י אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: And he continued, “Why is my lord pursuing his servant? What have I done? What evil is in my hand?
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul.
David was a servant of Saul.
David said, “Why does my lord chase his servant?”
David asked, “What have I done?”
David said, “What evil is in my hand?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֛ה אֲדֹנִ֥י רֹדֵ֖ף אַחֲרֵ֣י עַבְדּ֑וֹ כִּ֚י מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתִי וּמַה־ בְּיָדִ֖י רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: Now please, may my lord the king hear the words of his servant: If the LORD has stirred you up against me, then may He accept an offering. But if men have done it, may they be cursed in the presence of the LORD! For today they have driven me away from sharing in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods.’
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul, the king of Israel.
David was Saul’s servant.
David said, “Please listen to my words, my lord the king.”
David said, “If the LORD has stirred you up against me, may the LORD accept an offering.”
David said, “But if men have stirred you up against me, may those men be cursed before the LORD.”
David said, “Today these men have driven me away from sharing in the inheritance of the LORD.”
David said, “They say to me, ‘Go, serve other gods.’”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה יִֽשְׁמַֽע־ נָא֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֣י עַבְדּ֑וֹ אִם־ יְהוָ֞ה הֱסִֽיתְךָ֥ בִי֙ יָרַ֣ח מִנְחָ֔ה וְאִ֣ם׀ בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֗ם אֲרוּרִ֥ים הֵם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־ גֵרְשׁ֣וּנִי הַיּ֗וֹם מֵהִסְתַּפֵּ֜חַ בְּנַחֲלַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֵ֥ךְ עֲבֹ֖ד אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִֽים׃

passages.text: So do not let my blood fall to the ground far from the presence of the LORD. For the king of Israel has come out to look for a flea, like one who hunts a partridge in the mountains.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul, the king of Israel.
David was innocent.
David asked Saul not to kill him far from the presence of the LORD.
David said, “Do not let my blood fall to the ground away from the LORD.”
David explained that Saul, the king, was searching for him.
David compared himself to a flea.
David said Saul was hunting him like someone hunts a partridge in the mountains.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה אַל־ יִפֹּ֤ל דָּֽמִי֙ אַ֔רְצָה מִנֶּ֖גֶד פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־ יָצָ֞א מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְבַקֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־ פַּרְעֹ֣שׁ אֶחָ֔ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יִרְדֹּ֥ף הַקֹּרֵ֖א בֶּהָרִֽים׃

passages.text: Then Saul replied, “I have sinned. Come back, David my son. I will never harm you again, because today you considered my life precious. I have played the fool and have committed a grave error!”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to David.
Saul said, “I have sinned.”
Saul said, “Come back, David my son.”
Saul said, “I will not harm you again.”
Saul said, “Today you saw my life as valuable.”
Saul said, “You spared me.”
Saul said, “I acted foolishly.”
Saul said, “I made a very great mistake.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ שָׁא֨וּל חָטָ֜אתִי שׁ֣וּב בְּנִֽי־ דָוִ֗ד כִּ֠י לֹֽא־ אָרַ֤ע לְךָ֙ ע֔וֹד תַּ֠חַת אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָקְרָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֛י בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה הִנֵּ֥ה הִסְכַּ֛לְתִּי וָאֶשְׁגֶּ֖ה הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: “Here is the king’s spear,” David answered. “Let one of the young men come over and get it.
passages.sermon:
David spoke.
David said, “Here is the king’s spear.”
David told them to send one of the young men.
David said, “Let him come and take the spear.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַן דָּוִד֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר הִנֵּ֖ה הַחֲנִית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְיַעֲבֹ֛ר אֶחָ֥ד מֵֽהַנְּעָרִ֖ים וְיִקָּחֶֽהָ׃

passages.text: May the LORD repay every man for his righteousness and faithfulness. For the LORD delivered you into my hand today, but I would not stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed.
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul.
David was a servant of God.
David said, “May the LORD repay each person for his righteousness.
May the LORD repay each person for his faithfulness.
Today the LORD gave you into my hand.
You are the king of Israel.
You are the LORD’s anointed.
I did not harm you.
I refused to raise my hand against the LORD’s anointed.”
passages.original: וַֽיהוָה֙ יָשִׁ֣יב לָאִ֔ישׁ אֶת־ צִדְקָת֖וֹ וְאֶת־ אֱמֻנָת֑וֹ אֲשֶׁר֩ נְתָנְךָ֨ יְהוָ֤ה׀ הַיּוֹם֙ בְּיָ֔ד וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֔יתִי לִשְׁלֹ֥חַ יָדִ֖י בִּמְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: As surely as I valued your life today, so may the LORD value my life and rescue me from all trouble.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul.
David had spared Saul’s life.
David said he valued Saul’s life that day.
David said, “I saw your life as important today.”
David asked the LORD to see his own life as important.
David said, “May the LORD value my life.”
David asked the LORD to rescue him from all trouble.
David said, “May the LORD save me from every danger.”
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר גָּדְלָ֧ה נַפְשְׁךָ֛ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה בְּעֵינָ֑י כֵּ֣ן תִּגְדַּ֤ל נַפְשִׁי֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְיַצִּלֵ֖נִי מִכָּל־ צָרָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Saul said to him, “May you be blessed, David my son. You will accomplish great things and will surely prevail.” So David went on his way, and Saul returned home.
passages.sermon:
Saul spoke to David.
Saul called David his son.
Saul said, “May you be blessed, David my son.”
Saul said, “You will do great things.”
Saul said, “You will surely succeed.”
David left and went on his way.
Saul returned to his home.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד בָּר֤וּךְ אַתָּה֙ בְּנִ֣י דָוִ֔ד גַּ֚ם עָשֹׂ֣ה תַעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְגַ֖ם יָכֹ֣ל תּוּכָ֑ל וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ לְדַרְכּ֔וֹ וְשָׁא֖וּל שָׁ֥ב לִמְקוֹמֽוֹ׃פ
